name: Optimize AutoData generation for speed, rate-limit safety, and quality

description: Baseline AutoData benchmark with mocked DSPy workloads covering split and signature generation, output balancing, and simulated rate-limit pressure.

asi.hypothesis: Current pipeline likely wastes time in duplicate detection, oversized request bursts, and oversample rewrite behavior.
asi.benchmark_workload: mocked split+signature AutoData generation with simulated safe concurrency of 4
observed_bottlenecks: quality baseline already achieves full production and zero balance error

description: Tried bounded in-flight request batching plus cached fingerprints and deferred balanced writes; benchmark improved strongly but a new test was invalid and checks failed.

asi.hypothesis: Capping concurrent request bursts, avoiding O(n^2) duplicate scans, and skipping intermediate oversample writes should improve speed and reduce rate-limit failures.
asi.rollback_reason: New test used a predictor that always returned the same row, so duplicate filtering prevented reaching n and caused a false failure.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the code changes, fix the test to emit unique rows, and rerun benchmark.
asi.learned: The code-path changes benchmark well: total_ms 69.338 -> 63.268 and simulated rate_limit_failures 5 -> 0 before revert.

description: Add safer bounded in-flight request batching, cache row fingerprints for O(1) duplicate detection, defer oversample writes until final balanced selection, and prefer higher-quality ties during balanced subsampling.

asi.hypothesis: AutoData can be both faster and safer by capping burst concurrency, eliminating repeated duplicate scans, and avoiding wasted oversample disk writes.
asi.rate_limit_strategy: new max_inflight_requests cap (default 4) bounds burst size independently from local thread count
asi.quality_preservation: kept validation/duplication checks; balanced selection now prefers higher-quality rows on ties
learned: Simulated rate-limit failures dropped from 5 to 0
Split mode gained most from the changes

description: Tried caching field specs, validators, and predictor scaffolding on AutoData instances to reduce Python overhead, but the measured gain was not better than the current best.

asi.hypothesis: Memoizing validators/specs/predictors may shave Python overhead in repeated generation stages.
asi.rollback_reason: Benchmark regressed versus the kept bounded-concurrency/fingerprint/write-deferral version (63.796ms vs 63.382ms).
asi.next_action_hint: Try structural output-generation changes, especially reducing fallback calls or improving batch failure recovery.
asi.learned: Caching scaffolding had negligible or negative effect in this workload; main wins likely already came from request budgeting and avoiding wasted work.

description: Retested batched write_rows plus balanced-final write_rows usage to check whether the small apparent improvement was real; rerun landed worse than the current kept result, so treat it as noise.

asi.hypothesis: Batch-appending rows with a single fsync may slightly reduce output rewrite overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Follow-up run did not beat the kept version; observed gain appears within noise for this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Focus next on changes that reduce model-call structure or signature-mode write overhead, not micro-IO tweaks alone.
asi.learned: write_rows batching may help marginally, but the effect was not stable enough to keep over the existing bounded-concurrency win.

description: Batch multi-row dataset writes with a single append/fsync and use batched writes for signature-mode acceptance and final balanced rewrites, cutting persistence overhead without weakening validation or quality gates.

asi.hypothesis: Persistence overhead still matters, especially in signature mode where rows were fsynced one-by-one.
asi.write_strategy: write_rows now appends JSONL/CSV/parquet batches efficiently; signature mode accumulates accepted rows per parsed batch before writing
asi.quality_preservation: row validation, duplicate filtering, and balancing behavior unchanged
learned: Signature-mode time dropped materially (16.925ms -> 14.261ms vs kept version)
Total benchmark improved to 60.865ms with rate_limit_failures still 0
This resembles DataDesigner-style staged batching while keeping DSPy semantics

description: Batch accepted output-row persistence in split mode so batch successes and single-row fallbacks are appended once per iteration instead of fsyncing each accepted row individually.

asi.hypothesis: Split-mode output generation still pays unnecessary per-row persistence overhead; buffering accepted rows per iteration should improve throughput without changing validation or fallback semantics.
asi.quality_preservation: Acceptance logic, validation, duplicate handling, and fallback behavior are unchanged; only write batching changed.
learned: rate_limit_failures remained 0 and quality metrics stayed flat
asi.next_action_hint: Next promising path is structural retry improvement for output generation, e.g. re-batching failed outputs through smaller batches before single-item fallback.

description: Tried replacing full pending-list re-filtering in split output generation with incremental next_pending tracking to reduce list churn, but it did not beat the current best.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding repeated full pending list reconstruction should reduce Python overhead in output generation loops.
asi.rollback_reason: Benchmark regressed slightly versus the kept version (58.040ms vs 57.665ms), so the change is not worth keeping.
asi.next_action_hint: Try a more structural output retry improvement, such as smaller-batch retries before single-row fallback, or target signature-mode setup overhead.
asi.learned: The existing simple pending-index filtering is already efficient enough relative to other costs in this workload.

description: Tried chunk-level batched persistence in signature mode to reduce write frequency further, but it did not beat the current best overall result.

asi.hypothesis: Accumulating accepted signature-mode rows across the whole chunk before writing may trim fsync overhead further.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric was slightly worse than the kept best (57.728ms vs 57.665ms), so this is not a clear win.
asi.next_action_hint: Pursue structural output retry improvements next, especially smaller-batch retries before single-row fallback, or add a benchmark scenario that exercises partial output failures without weakening quality constraints.
asi.learned: Signature-mode write batching may be near its local optimum already; additional batching gave only a tiny, non-winning change.

description: Tried smaller-batch output retries before single-row fallback to better handle partial batch failures in real APIs, but it slightly regressed on the current benchmark.

asi.hypothesis: A staged retry ladder (full batch -> smaller retry batches -> single-row fallback) should reduce expensive single-call fallback in partial-failure scenarios without weakening quality checks.
asi.rollback_reason: Current benchmark does not exercise partial output failures, so the extra retry path added overhead without improving the primary metric (57.858ms vs best 57.665ms).
asi.next_action_hint: Either add a representative partial-output-failure benchmark scenario and reinitialize, or focus on always-hot paths like generator setup, signature-mode validation, or configurable durability tradeoffs.
asi.learned: The retry-ladder idea remains plausible for production resilience, but it is not justified by the present benchmark target.

description: Remove redundant split-output write de-dup bookkeeping: each pending index is only accepted once per iteration, so the extra written_indices set was unnecessary overhead on the hot path.

asi.hypothesis: The split output hot path can be simplified further by removing bookkeeping that no longer protects any real duplicate-write case.
asi.quality_preservation: Validation, fallback behavior, produced rows, diversity, and balance semantics are unchanged; only redundant per-acceptance state tracking was removed.
learned: rate_limit_failures remained 0 with no quality regressions
asi.next_action_hint: Keep targeting always-hot per-row overhead in output and signature acceptance loops before pursuing benchmark-cold resilience paths.

description: Tried removing growth of the seed-row bookkeeping lists in input and signature generation now that duplicate detection uses fingerprint sets, but it regressed on the benchmark.

asi.hypothesis: Avoiding appends to now-redundant seed bookkeeping lists should reduce hot-path overhead in input and signature generation.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed versus the kept best (58.488ms vs 57.369ms), so the simplification is not paying off in this workload.
asi.next_action_hint: Focus next on tighter per-row validation/parsing overhead or benchmark-visible setup costs rather than removing minor list bookkeeping.
asi.learned: Some apparently redundant list state may still interact favorably with current Python execution patterns; not all simplifications are wins.

description: Increase split output-generation batch size from the old 10-row cap to a moderate 16-row cap, reducing model round-trips while keeping validation, fallback, and quality checks unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: The split output path is still round-trip bound; a moderately larger typed output batch should improve throughput without changing data semantics.
asi.quality_preservation: No validation or balancing logic changed; only the number of rows requested per output batch increased to a still-conservative 16.
learned: signature_ms stayed roughly flat, confirming the win is concentrated in split output batching
asi.next_action_hint: Probe whether similarly moderate batching wins exist elsewhere, but avoid pushing batch sizes so high that real prompt size or partial-failure risk would outweigh the gain.

description: Increase split output-generation batch cap again from 16 to 20 rows; this further reduces round-trips on the hot typed-batch path while preserving all validation and fallback behavior.

asi.hypothesis: The split output path still benefits from a slightly larger but still moderate batch cap, with throughput gains outweighing batching overhead.
asi.quality_preservation: Only batch size changed; validation, balancing, duplicate handling, and fallback semantics are unchanged.
learned: quality and rate-limit metrics remained stable
asi.next_action_hint: Continue probing the split output batch-size frontier cautiously; stop once gains flatten or regress to avoid overfitting or unrealistic prompt growth.

description: Increase split output-generation batch cap from 20 to 24 rows; the larger typed batch still improves the hot split-output path slightly without changing validation or fallback behavior.

asi.hypothesis: There is still a little headroom in split output batching before prompt-size or failure risk dominates.
asi.quality_preservation: Only the typed output batch cap changed; validation, balancing, duplicate handling, and fallback semantics are unchanged.
learned: quality and rate-limit metrics stayed flat
asi.next_action_hint: One more cautious probe of the batch-size frontier may be worthwhile, but stop quickly if gains flatten or reverse to avoid overfitting.

description: Probed a higher split output-generation batch cap of 28 rows to find the batching frontier, but it regressed versus the current best.

asi.hypothesis: A somewhat larger typed output batch might still reduce round-trips enough to beat the 24-row cap.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed versus the kept 24-row cap (50.104ms vs 49.712ms), indicating the batching frontier has likely been crossed.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop increasing the split output batch cap; pivot to other hot-path overheads or at most confirm 24 with a rerun if needed.
asi.learned: 24 rows appears near the sweet spot for the current workload; pushing to 28 adds enough overhead or prompt cost to lose the gain.

description: Raise per-request row caps for input generation and signature-mode generation from 10 to a moderate 12 rows, reducing round-trips on both always-hot generation paths while preserving validation and diversity checks.

asi.hypothesis: Input and signature generation are still round-trip bound; modestly larger row counts per request should improve throughput similarly to the split output batching win without pushing prompts to extreme sizes.
asi.quality_preservation: Only request row caps changed; duplicate filtering, validation, balancing, diversity prompts, and fallback behavior are unchanged.
learned: rate_limit_failures remained 0 and output quality metrics stayed flat
asi.next_action_hint: Probe whether 12 is the new sweet spot or whether a small further increase in input/signature row caps still helps before prompt-size costs dominate.

description: Increase input-generation and signature-generation request row caps from 12 to 14; the modestly larger requests further reduce round-trips while preserving validation, diversity, and balance behavior.

asi.hypothesis: The input and signature paths still have a bit more batching headroom beyond 12 rows per request before prompt-size costs dominate.
asi.quality_preservation: Only request row caps changed; duplicate filtering, validation, balancing, diversity prompting, and fallback behavior are unchanged.
learned: quality and rate-limit metrics remained stable
asi.next_action_hint: One more cautious probe of these row caps may be worthwhile, but stop quickly if gains flatten to benchmark noise or reverse.

description: Increase input-generation and signature-generation request row caps from 14 to 16; the larger but still moderate requests sharply reduce round-trips on both hot generation paths while preserving validation and diversity behavior.

asi.hypothesis: The input and signature paths still have meaningful batching headroom at 16 rows per request, and round-trip savings will outweigh any prompt-size overhead.
asi.quality_preservation: Only request row caps changed; duplicate filtering, validation, balancing, diversity prompting, and fallback behavior are unchanged.
learned: quality and rate-limit metrics remained stable
asi.next_action_hint: Continue cautiously probing this batching frontier, but confirm the next step carefully because prompt-size cliffs may appear quickly beyond this point.

description: Increase input-generation and signature-generation request row caps from 16 to 18; the larger requests reduce round-trips further and improve total throughput while preserving validation, diversity, and balance behavior.

asi.hypothesis: The input and signature paths still have batching headroom at 18 rows per request, and round-trip savings continue to dominate prompt-size overhead.
asi.quality_preservation: Only request row caps changed; duplicate filtering, validation, balancing, diversity prompting, and fallback behavior are unchanged.
learned: signature_ms rose slightly from 9.089ms to 9.228ms but overall gain was strong
quality and rate-limit metrics remained stable
asi.next_action_hint: Probe 20 rows cautiously or consider asymmetric caps for input vs signature mode if one path starts flattening sooner than the other.
